narrative.title: The Field Scout's Sprint Budget
narrative.scenario: A rescue scout traverses n ridge markers and may leap over up to k markers in a single bound. Crossing from marker i to marker j burns stamina equal to the absolute elevation difference between them. The expedition lead needs the least-strenuous itinerary across the ridge, so the scout's wrist computer must report the minimum stamina for the full traverse.
narrative.inputFormat: Integers n and k, plus an array height of n integers giving each marker's elevation.
narrative.outputFormat: Return the minimum total stamina to travel from marker 0 to marker n-1 with jumps of at most k.

testCases.explanation: 0 to 2 costs |10-30| = 20, then 2 to 3 costs |30-10| = 20 — total 40.
Hop 0 to 3 directly (|10-20| = 10), then 3 to 4 (|60-20| = 40) — total 50; every other route lands at 50 or worse.

hintLevels: Level 1: Same landing logic as the two-hop frog, but now every landing spot within k steps back competes.
Level 2: best[i] = min over j in 1..k of best[i-j] + |h[i] - h[i-j]|.
Level 3: Keep the inner loop bounded by i so the first k markers are handled without sentinel values.
